label: D2 rare a2->S1; larger when switching to a2, belief favours S1, last unrewarded
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * (belief > 0.5) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * belief_cover ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and almost only after a rare a2->S1 transition (choice and state are both observed at D2). Zero at D1 and GO. Its size within those events depends on observed history. It is larger when the ideal-observer belief favours S1 being good (graded belief_lo plus a step at belief > 0.5) and grows slightly with belief_cover. It is larger when the a2 choice was a switch from a1 (+0.35). It is smaller when the previous trial was rewarded (-0.22), when the previous trial was also a2->S1 (-0.16), and later in the episode (about -0.04 per decile). Dev R^2 beyond timing: 0.14 for the a2->S1 indicator alone, 0.58 for all 8 terms. Test: 0.59. That beats the all-cue reference ceiling of 0.53 (which includes model value and policy), so leaving out model outputs costs nothing here. No future or hidden variables are used. The remaining misses are under-predicted peaks (actual about 1.5-1.9 vs predicted 0.3-0.7), mostly after a1 S1 u.

issues: Minor overclaim on the switch effect. The +0.35 'switching from a1' boost applies only when the previous a1 trial went unrewarded. Adding A*(prev_action==1)*(prev_reward==1) gives weights of +0.56 for prev a1, -0.19 for prev rewarded and -0.46 for the interaction, so a switch to a2 after a rewarded a1 trial gets roughly no boost. Test R^2 is the same (0.593), but the label's separate 'switch' and 'last unrewarded' effects are really one interaction.

The 'belief > 0.5 step' adds little once graded belief_lo is in the model. belief_lo alone with A scores 0.42 test, and belief > 0.5 alone with A scores 0.34. belief_cover adds almost nothing (A alone 0.152 -> 0.158 test), so 'a little more belief_cover' is negligible.

'Loses nothing vs the model-output version' is based only on the 0.53 additive-table ceiling. The earlier value/policy explanation's actual score was not compared, so how much the observed-only version loses is not measured directly.

Remaining error is under-predicted peaks inside a2->S1 D2 events (actual 1.5-2.3 vs predicted 0.8-1.1). misses shows no systematic phase x previous-trial class: all mean errors are below 0.035, D1 and GO are exactly 0 actual, and the fit's small offset there (+0.008) comes from the intercept. The leftover looks like a scale or nonlinearity issue, not a missing condition.
